title: FOMC decision (meeting January 25-26, 2028) — the calendar's first 2028 entry, and the Committee's annual organizational meeting
source: EST: TWO INDEPENDENT BOARD PRIMARIES AGREE, both fetched raw and parsed by this session on 2026-09-09. (1) federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, stamp 'Last Update: August 19, 2026'): the note below the 2027 panel reads verbatim 'Note: A two-day meeting is scheduled for January 25-26, 2028. Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it.' (2) federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/fomc-blackout-period-calendar.pdf (HTTP 200, 98,013 bytes) carries a JANUARY 2028 page whose content stream this session inflated and whose shaded cells it decoded by rectangle geometry: 2028-01-15 through 2028-01-27 are shaded as blackout dates and 2028-01-25/26 sit inside the red 'FOMC meeting days' box. THE SECOND DOCUMENT MARKS THE MEETING GRAPHICALLY AND IS NOT A RESTATEMENT OF THE FIRST. Weekday arithmetic computed, not assumed: 2028-01-01 is a Saturday, so 2028-01-25 is a Tuesday and 2028-01-26 a Wednesday, and the decision is Wednesday 2028-01-26 per this calendar's standing convention of keying an FOMC entry to the decision day (fomc-2027-12-08 for 'December 7-8'). Independently corroborated by rule: 20 of the 21 January meetings 2007-2027 begin on the LAST TUESDAY of January (sole exception 2012-01-24), and 2028-01-25 is the last Tuesday of January 2028. No SEP asterisk, consistent with every January in the record. Kalshi's KXFEDDECISION-28JAN ladder (read direct 2026-09-09) closes 2028-01-26T18:59:00Z and expires 19:05:00Z = 13:59/14:05 ET under EST, a venue keying the same decision date; a venue corroborates, it never promotes. HELD AT ESTIMATE BECAUSE THE PRIMARY DISCLAIMS ITSELF, not for want of evidence: the same page states every meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it, which for this one is the December 7-8, 2027 meeting. The 14:00 ET statement time is the Board's standing convention and is not stated on the calendar page. notes: THE CALENDAR'S HORIZON. This is the first and only 2028 entry the calendar carries; the +/-5-day corridor 2028-01-21 -> 2028-01-31 is empty by construction, as is every window after 2027-12-31. THE MEETING'S DISTINCTIVE CONTENT IS INSTITUTIONAL AND SOURCED, NOT TRADEABLE. federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomc.htm (fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 95,433 bytes) states verbatim 'Committee membership changes at the first regularly scheduled meeting of the year' and publishes the 2028 rotation: voting Reserve Bank members New York, Cleveland, Boston, St. Louis, Kansas City (alternates New York FVP, Chicago, Philadelphia, Dallas, Minneapolis) -- so this meeting seats a new voting roster. The Board's live Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy (FOMC_LongerRunGoals.pdf, HTTP 200, 63,302 bytes, 'Adopted effective January 24, 2012; as reaffirmed effective January 27, 2026') states verbatim that the Committee 'intends to review these principles and to make adjustments as appropriate at its annual organizational meeting each January, and to undertake roughly every 5 years a thorough public review'. MEASURED, THAT CONTENT IS WORTH NOTHING: the 14 meetings the Board's own calendar attaches a Longer-Run Goals statement to run a 0.927% mean absolute S&P decision-day move against 0.926% for the other 141, permutation P = 0.9991. The January cell is likewise the table's null -- 0.923% (n=18) against a pooled 0.925% across all 156 decision days 2007-2026, and 0.896% for the 19-meeting January class against 0.931% for the rest, P = 0.881.
